summary.text: Michael Lazzara is a Republican member of the North Carolina State Senate who has represented District 6 since January 2021 and is on the ballot for re-election on November 3, 2026.
A U.S. Marine Corps veteran and business owner, he previously served on the Jacksonville City Council.

paragraphs.text: Michael Lazzara was born in Palermo, Sicily, Italy, and served in the U.S. Marine Corps, according to Ballotpedia.
In a 2020 Ballotpedia survey, he said he arrived at Camp Lejeune in 1982 after Parris Island, completed a four-year enlistment in 1986 and made Jacksonville his home as a small business owner.
His career experience includes owning and serving as president of Lazzara Enterprises.

Lazzara said in the survey that he was elected to the Jacksonville City Council in 2005 and served as mayor pro tem for 12 years, and that he served as president of the North Carolina League of Municipalities.
He assumed office in the State Senate on January 1, 2021, succeeding Harry Brown.

For 2025-2026, Ballotpedia lists him as chair of the Appropriations on Department of Transportation and Transportation committees and as a member of the Finance, Judiciary, Rules and Operations of the Senate and State and Local Government committees.
His 2020 survey named K-12 and community college education, protecting the military footprint, public safety and lower taxes among his key messages.
